subject: Emergency triage: request to retain ops artifacts for live investigation
messages:
From: Elena Kovacs <elena.kovacs@aperturehealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-21 09:12 -0800
Subject: urgent: can you hold logs for our live triage?

Hi Ben,

We're in an active triage for a model hallucination reported on our payments flow. Our engineering lead asked if Redwood can preserve the last 48 hours of request/response traces and the associated KV cache slices for our tenant while we debug. The standard retention would purge some of that data tonight and we need a short holding window to reproduce.

Can you escalate a short, timeboxed retention exception (48-72 hours) for Aperture Health's tenant? We need assurance that the data will be deleted automatically after the window and that access will be restricted to a small set of operators.

I've attached a one-page incident summary.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Kovacs
Head of Platform Engineering, Aperture Health
Elena.Kovacs@aperturehealth.com

Attachments: aperture_incident_summary_20261121.pdf

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: elena.kovacs@aperturehealth.com
Date: 2026-11-21 09:36 -0800
Subject: Fwd: urgent: can you hold logs for our live triage?

Team — forwarding Aperture Health's ask. They specifically want the last ~48 hours of request/response traces, the model input/output payloads for the payment flow, and the small set of KV cache prefixes tied to that tenant. They request a 48-72 hour, fully-audited exception with automatic deletion afterwards.

Questions for approval:
- Legal/security OK with timeboxed snapshot for debugging?
- SRE: what is the minimal artifact set to collect (preserve vs full snapshot)?
- Ops: audit & scoped access controls during the window?

Elena, copying our security and SRE leads to move fast. I'll patch together an approval doc once I get the thumbs up.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-21 10:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: urgent: can you hold logs for our live triage?

Ben — thanks for the heads up. Short answer: we can authorize a timeboxed exception for forensic debugging but it needs to meet strict controls: 

- Exception window limited to 72 hours maximum and must be non-extendable without another approval.
- Access must be restricted to named operators; all access logged with audit trail and reason for each access.
- Data must be tagged in our system as "forensic-slice" and scheduled for automated purge at end-of-window.
- We need a minimal scope. Prefer a filtered slice (IDs/timestamp range + specific request traces) instead of full tenant dumps.

If SRE confirms the exact artifacts, I'll sign the approval PDF and route to Compliance for record. Also request that Ben capture the exact query used to extract the slice so we can reproduce and validate deletion.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-21 11:18 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: urgent: can you hold logs for our live triage?

Short technical note from SRE:
We can produce a timeboxed forensic slice for the tenant. Recommended artifacts (minimal):
- Request/response traces for the payments route only (service: payments-service; last 48 hours).
- Model IO payloads for requests where trace_id matches payments route (filter by route_id + timestamps).
- KV cache prefixes for the tenant limited to the 3 keys that map to the payments-context (we'll enumerate keys).
- Execution environment metadata (model variant, quantization profile, node id).

Process: we'll create a read-only snapshot stored in an ops bucket with ACLs restricted to the named people. Snapshot will be encrypted and labeled with retention TTL. We'll attach a small manifest file and log all accesses to the snapshot (audit ID: audit-20261121-APTR).

Attachments: ops_log_slice_20261121.tar.gz.stub (placeholder)

Connor O'Brien
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: elena.kovacs@aperturehealth.com
Date: 2026-11-21 13:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: urgent: can you hold logs for our live triage?

Thanks — procedures below. I approve a 72-hour, non-extendable exception for Aperture Health pending the following be completed before we release the snapshot:
1) Ben to confirm exact time range and route IDs (so extraction is narrowly scoped).
2) Connor to provide manifest with the extraction query and list of keys included.
3) Laura to sign approval PDF (records will be kept in Compliance folder).
4) CS (Marissa) to confirm that Aperture Health acknowledges deletion schedule and limited-access list.

Once those are done I'll sign the operational request and notify billing/security. Access will be via temporary RBAC token tied to audit-20261121-APTR.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Support Operations

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, elena.kovacs@aperturehealth.com
Date: 2026-11-23 16:40 -0800
Subject: RE: Emergency triage: request to retain ops artifacts for live investigation

All — quick status and final approvals.

What I did:
- Confirmed time range with Aperture: 2026-11-19T22:00:00Z through 2026-11-21T22:00:00Z (48 hours).
- Confirmed route: payments-service route_id=payments-v3.
- Connor created a filtered snapshot and uploaded to ops-snapshots/audit-20261121-APTR/ with manifest (manifest.json).
- Manifest lists three KV prefixes (payments_ctx_v1:{tenant}, payments_ctx_v1:session, payments_cache:v2:{tenant}).

Approvals:
- Laura: security approval received (signed pdf attached).
- Rishi: support ops approved (see thread).
- Marissa: CS confirmed Aperture signed the Acknowledgement Form.

Links & artifacts:
- Snapshot (read-only): https://ops.internal/snapshots/audit-20261121-APTR (RBAC enforced)
- JIRA: SUP-4521
- Attached: retention-exception-approval.pdf (signed by Laura), ops_log_slice_20261121.tar.gz.stub

Next steps:
- Snapshot TTL set to 72 hours from upload (auto-delete).
- Connor will forward the access audit after triage completes.
- Ben will follow up to confirm deletion.

Elena — please confirm when triage is complete and we'll close the loop.

Thanks everyone for quick turnaround.

—Ben
